text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: Each token I contribute returns only 0.75 to me but 3 total to the group, so keeping everything is individually dominant while full contribution is socially optimal. I'm leaning toward contributing something meaningful in round one to signal cooperative intent.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a classic public goods game: each token I put in returns 0.75 to each of 4 members, so contributing gives me back only 0.75 while benefiting others 2.25 total. Individually, zero contribution dominates, but full cooperation at 20 each yields the best group outcome—so I'm weighing short-term selfish logic against the benefits of sustained cooperation across rounds with unknown partners.

reply.thinking: Checking the math: keeping 10 and contributing 10 gives me 10 plus 0.75 of the 30 group total, which works out to 32.5. Since others averaged contributing around 6.67 each, I'll stick with cooperating and play 10 again this round.
